events.did: muttered 'Fucking EOs' and slammed the locker hard enough to make Rios wince
events.quote_anchor: The guard slammed the locker as he said it, hard enough that Rios winced. The anger, of course, wasn’t directed at her.

events.did: recognized the dizziness and laughter of the guards as hypoxia before anyone passed out
events.quote_anchor: Farley had recognized it as hypoxia before anyone passed out.

events.did: found that the latest Victor Vale mission was a setup, the whole place rigged to blow the moment they went in
events.quote_anchor: It was a setup, the whole place rigged to blow the moment they went in.

events.did: was the first EO ever offered a badge instead of a cell, and the first to accept
events.quote_anchor: She was the first EO to ever be offered a badge instead of a cell. Or at least, the first to accept.

events.did: came in from a mission still dressed in field gear, his visor cracked and the paint stripped from one temple
events.quote_anchor: He was still dressed in field gear—the tactical black plate wrapping around him like a second skin, helmet in the crook of one arm.

events.did: hauled a bound EO woman between them, blood dripping from her clothes and leaving a red trail
events.quote_anchor: As if on cue, two of his team came through the door looking similarly battered and hauling an EO between them.

events.did: disappeared when Stell prompted him to lower himself into a chair, then reappeared in it as camouflage
events.quote_anchor: Then, at his prompting, Noah had lowered himself into a chair, and proceeded to disappear.

events.did: stepped through the security checkpoint of EON, laughing with Noah at their shared 'Fucking EOs'
events.quote_anchor: They both laughed, and Rios felt the pressure easing in her chest as she stepped through the security checkpoint, the doors of EON breaking like a seal

relations.did: is one of the two EO field agents among EON's thirty-three agents
relations.quote_anchor: And of those thirty-three field agents, thirty-one were ordinary humans, and the other two were EOs.

relations.did: turned himself in to EON rather than being caught
relations.quote_anchor: His smile faltered. “They didn’t. I turned myself in.”

relations.did: offered Rios a badge instead of a cell, believing not every ExtraOrdinary deserved to be locked up
relations.quote_anchor: Stell had believed that not every ExtraOrdinary deserved to be locked up. He’d recognized the danger of their powers, left unchecked, but he saw the potential in them, too.

relations.did: is the other EO hiding in plain sight, an ally and an anchor to Rios
relations.quote_anchor: It was enough to know she was no longer the only one hiding in plain sight.

numbers.did: is a young man with the ability to alter the pressure of the air around him
numbers.quote_anchor: Apparently, there had been an incident with the EO in cell 008. A young man with the ability to alter the pressure of the air around him.

numbers.did: needed an hour of supplemental oxygen and two aspirin after the incident
numbers.quote_anchor: But an hour of supplemental oxygen and two aspirin later, he was in a foul mood.

numbers.did: had been sent into the field three times in search of Victor Vale
numbers.quote_anchor: Three times she’d been sent into the field in search of Victor Vale.

numbers.did: grew from the ten-person task force first formed by Stell six years before
numbers.quote_anchor: The department of ExtraOrdinary Observation and Neutralization had come a long way from the ten-person task force first formed by Stell six years before.

numbers.did: number eighty, of whom forty-seven are guards at the compound and thirty-three are field agents
numbers.quote_anchor: Of the eighty soldiers who now worked for EON, forty-seven were guards stationed at the compound, and thirty-three were agents in the field.

numbers.who: the EOs among EON's field agents
numbers.quote_anchor: And of those thirty-three field agents, thirty-one were ordinary humans, and the other two were EOs.
